reason: I don't hand real money to a finance app nobody's heard of, and this one has zero reviews and a broker partner they won't even name. The pet thing is cute, but I'd poke at the demo, not sign up for a paid real-money plan.
objection: If the agent makes a bad trade or a bad payment inside the limits I set, who eats the loss? Me, MyLiquid, or the broker nobody's named? Nothing here tells me.
would_change_my_mind: A named, licensed broker I already know holding the money (SIPC-covered), clear written terms on who's liable when the agent screws up, and a few months of real user reviews.
